title: Grapefruit juice, white, canned or bottled, unsweetened

content.title: About
content.content: Unsweetened white grapefruit juice is obtained by pressing ripe grapefruits and removing the pulp. The juice is typically light yellow, has a refreshing aroma and a slightly bitter taste. It is sold in canned jars or glass bottles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grapefruit was first cultivated in the early 19th century in the Caribbean as a hybrid of pomelo and sweet orange.
The juice is more than 90 % water and contains virtually no fat.
Its high citric acid content gives natural preservation without added preservatives.
In the United States grapefruit juice is often used in diet programs because of its low calorie count.
The juice can interact with certain medications, so medical advice is recommended.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: A 100‑ml serving provides about 30 mg of vitamin C, which supports immune function and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids help neutralize free radicals, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The acidity stimulates gastric juice production, aiding the digestion of food.

items.title: Low‑calorie beverage
items.content: One cup (250 ml) contains roughly 45 kcal, making it suitable for weight‑control diets.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Grapefruit juice can increase the effect of certain drugs (e.g., statins); consult a healthcare professional when taking medication.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to citrus fruits.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, use it in smoothies, cocktails, marinades, or as a base for sauces. If desired, add a touch of honey or fresh herbs to soften the bitterness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans or bottles in a cool, dark place. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5–7 days. Discard if the color, smell, or taste changes.
